youtube.title: The 64-packet queue that ate a megabyte #Shorts
youtube.description:
A 64-deep DTLS demux queue dropped burst records, SCTP retransmit storms truncated MiB chunk echoes — but only on the slightly slower FFI path. Queue is 4096 deep now, with a permanent queued tail-drop blast regression test. From the v0.44 consolidation: https://github.com/browser-grpc/grpc-over-datachannels

Built with Fish Audio

scenes.heading: The 64-packet queue
scenes.sub: A burst-loss bug story in 45 seconds
scenes.say: A sixty-four packet queue ate a megabyte message, and here is exactly how it happened.

scenes.heading: The symptom
bullets: 1 MiB chunked echo returns 13–15 of 16 chunks
Only on the Rust FFI path; the mirror passed
Flaky ~50% — always at exact 64 KiB boundaries
scenes.say: A one megabyte echo kept coming back short: thirteen to fifteen of sixteen chunks, always at exact sixty-four kibibyte boundaries, and only on the new Rust F F I path. The mirrored stack passed every time.

scenes.heading: The mechanism
bullets: FFI pump drains slightly slower → queue overflows
Dropped records → SCTP retransmit storm → final chunk lands first, message completes short
scenes.say: The peer demuxes D T L S records into a sixty-four deep queue that drops when full. The F F I pump drains slightly slower, the queue overflows mid-burst, S C T P retransmits race the final chunk, and the reassembler completes the message short.

scenes.heading: The fix
bullets: Permanent regression: queued tail-drop blast test in the Rust suite
Sweep after: 6/6 clean, at half the time
scenes.say: The queue is four thousand ninety-six deep now, and a queued tail-drop blast test lives in the Rust suite forever. Six of six clean sweeps, at half the previous time. Full story in the long video.
